guide.title: How to create the client (about 10 minutes)
guide.why: Google requires every app that reads Search Console and Analytics data to be registered in Google Cloud. This installation is yours, so you register it once.
guide.step1: Pick a project in Google Cloud and enable these three APIs: <sc>Search Console API</sc>, <data>Google Analytics Data API</data>, <admin>Google Analytics Admin API</admin>.
guide.step2: On <audience>Google Auth Platform → Audience</audience>, choose the External user type. While the app is in testing, only accounts on the Test users list can connect (others see “Error 403: access_denied”); publish the app for lasting use.
guide.step3: On <clients>Clients</clients>, create a client of the Web application type and add this address under Authorized redirect URIs:
guide.step4: Paste the client ID and secret below and save.

page_4xx.title: Page returns a 4xx error
page_4xx.description: These URLs return a client error such as 404. Visitors land on an empty page, search engines drop the page from the index and links pointing to it are wasted.
page_4xx.fix: If the page moved, add a 301 redirect to its new URL; if it was removed, update the internal links pointing to it. Restore the content if the page is still needed.

page_5xx.title: Page returns a server error (5xx)
page_5xx.description: The server could not produce these pages. If the error persists, Google slows down crawling and may drop the pages from its index.
page_5xx.fix: Find the error for these URLs in your server and application logs. If it is a temporary load problem, review capacity and caching, then run the audit again.

fetch_failed.title: Page could not be fetched
fetch_failed.description: The crawler could not connect to this URL or the response did not arrive in time. If search engines hit the same problem, the page is never indexed.
fetch_failed.fix: The reason is shown under the page. For timeouts check server response time, for host errors check DNS records, and for oversized responses check the page size.

redirect_loop.title: Redirect loop
redirect_loop.description: The redirects eventually lead back to a URL they started from. Browsers and search engines never reach the page.
redirect_loop.fix: Follow the URLs in the chain and make every redirect end at a final page that returns 200. Conflicting HTTP→HTTPS, www or trailing slash rules usually cause loops.

redirect_chain.title: Redirect chain
redirect_chain.description: The page passes through more than one redirect before reaching its final URL. Every hop slows loading and uses crawl budget.
redirect_chain.fix: Redirect the first URL straight to the final target with a single 301 and update internal links to the final URL.

blocked_by_robots.title: Page blocked by robots.txt
blocked_by_robots.description: These URLs were not crawled because of your robots.txt rules. That is fine if intended; otherwise the pages may appear in search results without content, or not at all.
blocked_by_robots.fix: Confirm that the block is intended. If the page should be indexed, remove or narrow the matching Disallow rule.

no_https.title: Site does not use HTTPS
no_https.description: The home page is served over insecure HTTP. Browsers mark the site as "not secure" and HTTPS is one of Google's ranking signals.
no_https.fix: Install a TLS certificate (for example from Let's Encrypt), 301-redirect every HTTP URL to its HTTPS counterpart and update canonicals, sitemaps and internal links to HTTPS.

robots_txt_unreachable.title: robots.txt cannot be read
robots_txt_unreachable.description: The request for robots.txt ended in a server error or connection problem. Google may pause crawling the site while this lasts.
robots_txt_unreachable.fix: Make sure /robots.txt returns 200 (or 404 when there is no file). Check that firewall or CDN rules do not block crawlers.

robots_txt_missing.title: No robots.txt file
robots_txt_missing.description: No robots.txt was found. The whole site is then considered crawlable, but without the file you cannot point crawlers to your sitemap or keep them out of areas you do not want crawled.
robots_txt_missing.fix: Add a robots.txt to the site root that at least lists your Sitemap and any areas that should not be crawled.

sitemap_missing.title: No XML sitemap found
sitemap_missing.description: No readable sitemap was found in robots.txt or at /sitemap.xml. A sitemap helps search engines find new and updated pages quickly.
sitemap_missing.fix: Create an XML sitemap that lists your indexable pages, reference it with a Sitemap line in robots.txt and submit it in Search Console.

sitemap_non_200.title: Sitemap URL does not return 200
sitemap_non_200.description: The sitemap lists URLs that redirect or return errors. Search engines trust the sitemap less and crawl budget is wasted.
sitemap_non_200.fix: Keep only canonical, indexable URLs that return 200 in the sitemap, and replace redirected URLs with their final targets.

canonical_broken.title: Canonical points to a broken page
canonical_broken.description: The canonical tag points to a URL that returns an error or redirects. Search engines ignore the tag and pick the version to index themselves.
canonical_broken.fix: Point the canonical to the final URL that returns 200 and is indexable. In most cases the page should reference itself (self-canonical).

canonical_multiple.title: Multiple canonical tags
canonical_multiple.description: The page has more than one canonical tag. When they conflict, search engines may ignore all of them.
canonical_multiple.fix: Keep a single canonical tag. Themes, plugins and SEO modules often each add one; make sure only one of them does.

sitemap_noindex.title: Noindex page in the sitemap
sitemap_noindex.description: The sitemap lists pages you do not want indexed. That sends search engines conflicting signals.
sitemap_noindex.fix: Remove the page from the sitemap if it should not be indexed; otherwise remove its noindex.

noindex_page.title: Page is excluded with noindex
noindex_page.description: These pages block indexing with meta robots or X-Robots-Tag. That can be deliberate, but accidentally removing important pages from search is a common mistake.
noindex_page.fix: Review the list and remove noindex from pages that should appear in search results.

canonicalized.title: Page declares another URL as canonical
canonicalized.description: The canonical tag of these pages points to a different URL, which search engines will most likely index instead. That is normal for filtered and parameterized pages.
canonicalized.fix: Check that the canonical target is right. If the page should rank on its own, make the canonical point to the page's own URL.

canonical_missing.title: No canonical tag
canonical_missing.description: The page does not declare a canonical URL. When parameter, www or trailing slash duplicates appear, search engines have to guess the right version.
canonical_missing.fix: Add a canonical tag with its own absolute URL to every indexable page.

title_missing.title: Missing title tag
title_missing.description: The page has no title tag or it is empty. The title is the clickable line in search results and one of the strongest on-page signals.
title_missing.fix: Write a unique title of about 50–60 characters that states the topic of the page and its main keyword.

title_duplicate.title: Duplicate title
title_duplicate.description: Several pages use the same title. Search engines struggle to tell them apart and the pages may compete for the same query.
title_duplicate.fix: Give every page a unique title that sets its content apart. If the pages really are the same, point one to the main version with a canonical.

title_too_long.title: Title too long
title_too_long.description: The title is longer than 60 characters and will most likely be cut off in search results, hiding important words.
title_too_long.fix: Shorten the title to under 60 characters, put the most important words first and move the brand name to the end.

title_too_short.title: Title too short
title_too_short.description: The title is shorter than 15 characters. Short titles do not describe the page well and miss ranking opportunities.
title_too_short.fix: Expand the title so it describes the topic of the page and its main keyword.

meta_description_missing.title: Missing meta description
meta_description_missing.description: The page has no meta description. Google then shows an arbitrary snippet from the page, which can lower the click-through rate in search results.
meta_description_missing.fix: Write a unique description of 120–160 characters that summarizes what the page offers and invites the click.

meta_description_duplicate.title: Duplicate meta description
meta_description_duplicate.description: Several pages use the same meta description, so they cannot be told apart in search results.
meta_description_duplicate.fix: Write a unique description for every page that describes its own content.

meta_description_too_long.title: Meta description too long
meta_description_too_long.description: The description is longer than 160 characters and will most likely be cut off in search results.
meta_description_too_long.fix: Shorten the description to under 160 characters and put the main message in the first sentence.

h1_missing.title: Missing H1 heading
h1_missing.description: The page has no H1 heading. The H1 tells visitors and search engines what the page is mainly about.
h1_missing.fix: Add a single H1 that states the main topic of the page; it usually matches the title tag.

h1_multiple.title: Multiple H1 headings
h1_multiple.description: The page has more than one H1. That is not an error, but it can blur what the page is mainly about.
h1_multiple.fix: Keep the main heading as the H1 and turn the others into H2 or H3.

content_duplicate.title: Duplicate content
content_duplicate.description: The text content of these pages is identical. Search engines show only one version and decide which one themselves.
content_duplicate.fix: Merge the copies and 301-redirect them, or use a canonical pointing to the main page on every version.

content_thin.title: Thin content
content_thin.description: The indexable page has fewer than 200 words. Pages with little content usually rank poorly and are rarely chosen as sources in AI answers.
content_thin.fix: Expand the page with original content that answers the searcher's question; if it adds no value, merge it with a similar page or noindex it.

images_missing_alt.title: Images without alt text
images_missing_alt.description: Some images have no alt text. People using screen readers cannot understand them and search engines cannot tell what they show.
images_missing_alt.fix: Add a short alt text describing every meaningful image. Use alt="" for decorative images.

lang_missing.title: Page language not declared
lang_missing.description: The html element has no lang attribute. Screen readers and translation tools have to guess the language of the page.
lang_missing.fix: Add a lang attribute with the page's language to the html element, for example lang="en".

broken_internal_links.title: Broken internal links
broken_internal_links.description: The page links to internal URLs that return errors. Visitors hit dead ends and crawl budget is wasted.
broken_internal_links.fix: Update the links to working URLs or remove them. The broken targets are listed under the page.

links_to_redirects.title: Internal links to redirects
links_to_redirects.description: The page links to internal URLs that redirect. Every click costs an extra request and some link value may be lost.
links_to_redirects.fix: Update internal links to point straight to the final URL.

nofollow_internal_links.title: Nofollow internal links
nofollow_internal_links.description: The page links to pages on your own site with nofollow. That stops internal link value from flowing and is rarely needed.
nofollow_internal_links.fix: Remove nofollow from internal links. If a page should not be indexed, use noindex on that page instead.

orphan_page.title: Orphan page
orphan_page.description: The page is in the sitemap but no crawled page links to it. Visitors cannot find it and search engines may treat it as unimportant.
orphan_page.fix: Link to the page from related category, menu or content pages; remove it from the sitemap if it is no longer needed.

deep_page.title: Deep page
deep_page.description: The page is more than 3 clicks away from the home page. Deep pages are crawled less often and are usually considered less important.
deep_page.fix: Give important pages a shorter link path from the home page, the menu or category pages.

slow_response.title: Slow server response
slow_response.description: Downloading the page took longer than 2 seconds. Slow responses hurt user experience and reduce how many pages search engines crawl.
slow_response.fix: Shorten response times with server-side caching, a CDN and database query optimization, and profile the application code behind these URLs.

page_too_large.title: Page too large
page_too_large.description: The HTML response is larger than 2 MB. Large pages load slowly and search engines may process only part of very large pages.
page_too_large.fix: Move inline scripts, styles and embedded data into separate files, and split long lists into pages.

viewport_missing.title: Missing viewport meta tag
viewport_missing.description: The page has no viewport meta tag, so mobile devices show it shrunk to desktop width. Google indexes sites by their mobile version.
viewport_missing.fix: Add a viewport meta tag with content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" to the page head and make sure the layout is responsive.

structured_data_invalid.title: Invalid structured data
structured_data_invalid.description: Some JSON-LD blocks on the page cannot be parsed. Invalid markup is not used for rich results and makes the page harder for AI systems to interpret.
structured_data_invalid.fix: Check the JSON-LD blocks with Google's Rich Results Test or the Schema.org validator and fix missing commas, quotes or escape characters.

structured_data_missing.title: No structured data
structured_data_missing.description: The indexable page has no JSON-LD structured data. Schema.org markup makes pages eligible for rich results and helps AI search engines understand your content.
structured_data_missing.fix: Add markup that fits the page type, such as Organization, Article, Product, FAQPage or BreadcrumbList.

ai_search_crawlers_blocked.title: AI search crawlers are blocked
ai_search_crawlers_blocked.description: robots.txt keeps AI search engines such as ChatGPT Search, Perplexity or Claude from fetching your pages, so they cannot cite your site in their answers.
ai_search_crawlers_blocked.fix: If you want to appear in AI answers, remove the Disallow rules for the blocked bots. You can manage search bots (such as OAI-SearchBot) separately from training bots (such as GPTBot).

ai_training_crawlers_blocked.title: AI training crawlers are blocked
ai_training_crawlers_blocked.description: robots.txt blocks bots that collect data to train models, such as GPTBot or Google-Extended. That is a policy choice and does not directly affect your visibility in AI search.
ai_training_crawlers_blocked.fix: No action is needed if the choice is deliberate. Allow these bots if you want your content to be used to train AI models.

llms_txt_missing.title: No llms.txt file
llms_txt_missing.description: The site has no /llms.txt. It is an emerging proposal that summarizes your most important pages for language models; it is not widely used yet.
llms_txt_missing.fix: Publish a Markdown file at /llms.txt that briefly introduces your site and links to its most important pages.

citability.description: How ready the indexable pages are to be cited in AI answers (score v1).

answer_first.title: Answer-first introduction
answer_first.recommendation: Open the page with a 30–80 word paragraph that answers the question directly and uses the topic terms of the heading.

question_headings.title: Question headings
question_headings.recommendation: Phrase at least a third of the H2/H3 headings as the questions users ask, with a short answer right below each.

structured_content.title: Lists and tables
structured_content.recommendation: Give steps, comparisons and specifications as lists or tables; aim for one structure per 600 words.

structured_data.title: Structured data
structured_data.recommendation: Add fitting JSON-LD (Article, FAQPage, HowTo, Product, Organization, BreadcrumbList) and fix invalid blocks.

authorship.title: Author and publisher
authorship.recommendation: Name the author with Person markup or a visible byline, and link the about and contact pages.

freshness.title: Freshness
freshness.recommendation: Update the page regularly and state dateModified/datePublished in JSON-LD or article meta tags.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.recommendation: Back claims with links to reliable sources and specific figures (rates, statistics, prices).

readability.title: Readability
readability.recommendation: Shorten sentences and use plain words; aim for an Ateşman or Flesch score of at least 50.

ai_crawler_access.title: AI search crawler access
ai_crawler_access.recommendation: Allow OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Claude-SearchBot and Claude-User to fetch the page in robots.txt.
